Marriage of the Lamb
MAIR-ij uhv thuh lam
noun
From Revelation 19:7; the consummation of the union between Christ the Lamb and His bride, the church.

📖 Biblical Definition

The marriage of the Lamb is the glorious consummation, at the end of the age, of the union between Christ the Lamb and His bride, the church. John hears the voice of a great multitude in heaven crying, Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints. The whole of Scripture has been a betrothal: the LORD took Israel to Himself as a husband; Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her, that He might sanctify and cleanse her, and present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing. The marriage supper of the Lamb is the wedding feast of that union made perfect—the everlasting joy of the redeemed in the immediate presence of their Lord, the bride forever with her Husband. Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. The dictionary honors the marriage of the Lamb as the great hope and end of the church’s history: that the Bridegroom who purchased His bride with His own blood will at last receive her to Himself, perfected and arrayed in His righteousness, to dwell with Him in unbroken joy for ever—the consummation toward which the whole story of redemption moves.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The consummation of the union between Christ the Lamb and His bride the church; the wedding feast of the redeemed with their Lord, the great hope and end of redemption.

MARRIAGE OF THE LAMB, the consummation of Christ’s union with the church.

The marriage of the Lamb is come, and His wife hath made herself ready (Rev 19:7).

The bride is arrayed in fine linen, the righteousness of saints.

Christ loved the church and gave Himself to present her glorious.

Blessed are they called to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9).

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 19:7 — "Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready."

Rev 19:9 — "And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God."

Eph 5:25 — "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;"

Rev 21:2 — "And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The marriage of the Lamb is reduced to mere symbol or sentimental imagery; Scripture proclaims the real consummation of Christ’s blood-bought union with His church.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the reduction of the marriage of the Lamb to mere symbol or sentimental imagery, emptied of its reality and its glory—a poetic flourish rather than the actual consummation toward which all redemption moves. But John heard the great multitude in heaven rejoice that the marriage of the Lamb is come (Rev 19:7); it is a real and coming event, the wedding of the Bridegroom and His bride, attested as the true sayings of God (Rev 19:9).

The principle to recover is the covenantal, blood-bought reality of Christ’s union with His church, perfected at the last. From the beginning the LORD has been Husband to His people; Christ loved the church and gave Himself for it, that He might present her to Himself a glorious church without spot or wrinkle (Eph 5:25-27). The marriage of the Lamb is that purpose brought to its consummation: the bride arrayed in fine linen, the righteousness of saints; the holy city coming down prepared as a bride adorned for her husband (Rev 21:2); the redeemed forever with their Lord. It is the great hope and end of the church’s history—not a sentiment but a certainty, toward which the whole story of redemption presses, and in which the Bridegroom shall at last receive His bride to unbroken joy for ever.
